engineering_assessments.assessment: Both tools pin the exact original acceptance digest and TRAIN/test-ineligible flags, then rehash every accepted NPZ they consume. The restoration tool requires882 files and8 shard directories. Replay binds collection plan bytes through acceptance, then manifest bytes through the plan, and requires every TRAIN sequence exactly once. Final replay also requires saved frame indices to equal positive in-range valid_frames[::25], matching the original collector. It records consumed NPZ digests. This is reuse of an immutable accepted input set, not a new acceptance of native shards, collector code, image pixels or all non-NPZ acceptance inputs.

Collector stores the initial box at predictions[0] and appends the current E0 returned box at predictions[frame], before recording that frame's candidate set. Candidates use previous=predictions[frame-1]. Replay correctly reconstructs the baseline from predictions[frames] and the same-frame TRAIN boxes, rather than comparing the previous state or a candidate proxy. box_iou computes ordinary image-space xywh IoU in float64 after shape, finite-value and positive-size checks.

Replay computes argmax over the frozen head's25 raw logits exactly as the saved training metrics do. Index0 is the learned no-match logit; index1..24 refers to the fixed cache candidate order. Head candidate scores average learned pair-match scores only across modalities with coverage==1, with entirely unobserved candidates masked to -infinity. Replay does not select using GT IoU, cached detector score, positive labels, a new threshold or a TEST statistic. Cached detector scores were used for the original two refinement parents, not for this M2 top1 decision.

Index0 leaves output_iou equal to current E0 IoU. A positive index replaces it with arrays.iou at chosen-1, with a consistency check against the selected saved candidate box and same-frame TRAIN annotation. The vectorized consistency check also checks candidate0 on no-match rows, but that value never replaces E0 on those rows. These overlaps are counterfactual instantaneous proposals on frozen E0 trajectories. They do not simulate changed history/templates, next-frame state, closed-loop recovery or online policy behavior.

Fit706 and holdout176 names must be disjoint and cover manifest.train exactly. Each cache stem is unique and assigned by those fixed names. Accepted labels use positive candidates at IoU>=0.5 with fully observed evidence; ambiguous/unobserved candidates remain -1. No-match truth requires observed evidence, no positive candidate and all candidate overlaps<0.1. Candidate-positive and no-match truth sets are mutually exclusive. The original verifier recomputed all labels against TRAIN annotations and bound the NPZ bytes into acceptance. This replay relies on that pinned acceptance rather than repeating the full verifier.

Supervised means any positive label. Correct means the chosen label is positive. Candidate truth counts sets with any positive candidate; candidate correct additionally requires a positive-index choice with positive chosen label. No-match correct requires truth index0 and chosen0. Rows without any positive label remain in all-state diagnostics but are excluded from supervised accuracy. Reliable>=0.5, lost<0.1 and uncertain[0.1,0.5) partition all checked finite E0 IoUs. selections/no_match_selected partition choices; better/worse/equal compare instantaneous selected IoU with baseline. Threshold-crossing counters are conditional on the baseline state and do not imply actual recovery.

engineering_assessments.assessment: Replay counters use the saved trainer's metric definitions and explicitly require holdout correct2747, supervised3450, candidate_correct2685 and no_match_correct62. Final source additionally compares BOTH fit and holdout supervised denominators, candidate denominators/correct counts, no-match denominators/correct counts and supervised top1 fraction with checkpoint.metrics, using1e-12 fraction tolerance. Thus3318/132 holdout denominators are now checked against the pinned checkpoint's saved metrics, rather than only emitted. Original accepted partition totals and saved epoch9 history agree with these expectations. 2685+62=2747 and3318+132=3450; fit10765/13074,10238/12281 and527/793 are also covered. This review establishes source equivalence and saved-metadata agreement; it did not reproduce these counts with a head forward.

Replay requires CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to be empty, loads the exact head checkpoint with map_location=cpu, and verifies epoch9, acceptance_sha256, protected E0 checkpoint identity against the collection plan and selection_partition=train_component_holdout. Those fields match the trainer's saved checkpoint schema. It constructs the current standard-CPU E0CandidateIdentity, strictly loads its state, sets eval and requires_grad=False, and runs under no_grad. It snapshots and exactly compares all state tensors, never creates an optimizer or calls backward, and requires CUDA never initialized. No E0 model or tracker is constructed. The restoration tool imports no torch and reads/hashes files only. The exact identity module source is pinned by replay; its imported ROI helper is not called by E0CandidateIdentity.forward. This is a source-level CPU/freeze assessment, not an executed model witness.

Replay writes a fresh output exclusively with open('x'), includes acceptance/plan/manifest/head/module/cache identities, zero optimizer updates and test-ineligible/scientific-false flags. It disclaims independent benchmark, semantic identity proof, upstream-independent holdout and online interventions. Restoration only prints a byte-verification receipt and explicitly excludes non-NPZ acceptance inputs and current source admission. Neither tool deploys source, collects new features, fits a model or selects a new TEST configuration.
